records.source_rule: An unnecessary intentional misplay of globally known trash well before the final rounds triggers Bomb Double Ignition.
records.learning_objective: Recognize the wasted strike as a Double Ignition trigger.
records.critical_variable: Alice deliberately bombs known trash while a safe discard exists and the game is not in the positional-misplay end window.
records.blind_answer: Bob and Cathy both blind-play Finesse Position.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Early known-trash bombing lacks the normal positional-misplay purpose.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat it as an ordinary positional misplay; timing rules reject that.
records.mutation: Move the action to the last rounds and positional-misplay meaning can become available.
records.noise: Question state is post-misplay and no longer leaves Alice's spent trash card in hand.

records.source_rule: Bombing for Ignition when an obvious clue-based Double Ignition was available upgrades the message to Triple Ignition.
records.learning_objective: Use action cost to infer the extra third Ignition.
records.critical_variable: Alice chooses a strike despite an available Replay Double Ignition.
records.blind_answer: Bob, Cathy, and Donald each perform an Ignition.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Stopping after two ignores the deliberately more expensive trigger.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Read it as ordinary Bomb DI; the cheaper available DI makes that insufficient.
records.mutation: Remove the cheaper clue-based trigger and the extra Triple signal disappears.
records.noise: Question state is post-bomb and no spent trash card remains in Alice's hand.

records.source_rule: Re-cluing globally known trash with no new cards and no Stall need is Poke Double Ignition.
records.learning_objective: Separate Poke DI from a legitimate Stall.
records.critical_variable: Alice has a known safe discard and the re-clue adds no cards.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The safe discard removes the Stall explanation.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat as Stall; ordinary discard availability rejects it.
records.mutation: Put Alice in a genuine stalling situation and the re-clue can be a Stall.
records.noise: Only the known-trash re-touch and safe-discard fact matter.

records.source_rule: A new known-trash clue that cannot be Trash Chop Move or Trash Push is Trash Double Ignition, preferred over rare bad-trash ejection.
records.learning_objective: Eliminate ordinary trash-clue meanings before selecting TDI.
records.critical_variable: The clue is off-chop and the cards a Trash Chop Move would protect are bad.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Neither Trash Push nor useful Trash Chop Move fits the visible position.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Infer a bad-trash ejection; Level 21 explicitly prioritizes TDI.
records.mutation: Put useful cards behind the trash and Trash Chop Move becomes plausible.
records.noise: No unrelated identity is needed beyond visible trash quality.

records.source_rule: A nonsensical Chop Move of a playable card with no independent reason is a Chop Move Ignition; Bob blind-plays and the receiver learns the moved card is playable.
records.learning_objective: Infer CMI from the strange playable Chop Move.
records.critical_variable: Cathy's moved chop is playable and Alice had ordinary Play Clues.
records.blind_answer: Bob blind-plays Finesse Position; Cathy then plays the Chop Moved card.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: A plain Early 5 Chop Move gives no reason for Bob's blind-play.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Bob can decline the blind-play; that misses the extra Ignition message.
records.mutation: Give the Chop Move a Good Touch or other ordinary justification and CMI disappears.
records.noise: Solution is a post-Ignition knowledge state rather than the official storyboard replay.

records.source_rule: Multi-card CMI requires a playable left boundary and a trash-or-same-hand-duplicate right boundary; both boundaries are Chop Moved.
records.learning_objective: Apply both multi-card boundary conditions and resulting knowledge.
records.critical_variable: Left boundary is playable red 2; right boundary is a duplicate blue 4.
records.blind_answer: Bob performs Ignition; Cathy plays the left boundary and treats the right boundary as known trash.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Both explicit boundary conditions are satisfied.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat as ordinary Trash Chop Move; Bob's Ignition evidence rejects that.
records.mutation: Make the right boundary neither trash nor a duplicate and the multi-card CMI is invalid.
records.noise: Solution shows post-Ignition playable/trash knowledge without action labels.

records.source_rule: Re-cluing a globally known playable card with no new cards and no Stall need is Replay Double Ignition.
records.learning_objective: Recognize useless replay as DI outside a stalling situation.
records.critical_variable: Alice can safely discard and the replay introduces no new card.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Safe discard availability removes the Stall explanation.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Call it Stall; not supported in this position.
records.mutation: Remove Alice's safe discard and a Stall explanation can return.
records.noise: Known playable state is explicit; no extra identities drive the answer.

records.source_rule: A playable Chop Move is not CMI when it has another good reason, including avoiding Good Touch violations.
records.learning_objective: Reject false-positive CMI when direct clues are genuinely worse.
records.critical_variable: Both direct Play Clues would touch an extra currently unhelpful card.
records.blind_answer: Do not blind-play; the Chop Move has an ordinary Good Touch justification.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The independent Good Touch benefit removes the uselessness required for CMI.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Blind-play as CMI; unjustified once the direct-clue cost is visible.
records.mutation: Remove the extra red 4 and yellow 2 touches and CMI can become valid.
records.noise: Bob's own hidden Finesse card is masked; only Cathy's visible hand matters.

records.source_rule: In ambiguous Double Ignition the first Ignition is Bob unless he already has a known play; the second is the last player with playable Finesse Position.
records.learning_objective: Select the two prescribed Ignition targets.
records.critical_variable: Bob already has another known-playable card while Cathy and Donald do not.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Bob is explicitly skipped when he already has a known play; Donald is the last playable target.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Choose Bob and Cathy; violates both target-selection rules.
records.mutation: Remove Bob's separate known play and the first target returns to Bob.
records.noise: Trigger itself is historical and omitted; only target state remains.

records.source_rule: When three or more cards are spanned by multi-card CMI, only leftmost and rightmost are Chop Moved; middle cards get no promise.
records.learning_objective: Protect the no-information status of middle cards.
records.critical_variable: Slots 3 and 5 are the two qualifying boundaries with slot 4 between them.
records.blind_answer: Slots 3 and 5 are Chop Moved; slot 4 is not and may be anything.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Source explicitly excludes middle cards from Chop Moved status.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat slot 4 as moved or constrained; unsupported by the rule.
records.mutation: Reduce the span to two cards and there is no middle-card issue.
records.noise: RU wording now uses Chop Moved as a state rather than a verb calque.

records.source_rule: The rank-5 Chop Move Ignition Interaction is turned off in End-Game.
records.learning_objective: Apply the End-Game exception instead of overgeneralizing Mid-Game CMI.
records.blind_answer: The Level 21 interaction alone does not force a blind-play.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Source explicitly disables the interaction in End-Game.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Blind-play automatically as Mid-Game CMI; exception rejects that.
records.mutation: Move the same position to Mid-Game and the interaction can force the CMI reading.
records.noise: The exact contrast card is stated by the question; no hidden inference is tested.

records.source_rule: Outside End-Game, a rank-5 clue focusing a 5 exactly one-away from chop has Play Clue interpretations turned off for the CMI Interaction.
records.learning_objective: Prefer the CMI interaction over a direct-play interpretation.
records.critical_variable: Mid-Game, a 5 exactly one-away from chop, and Alice skipped an expected clue to the moved card.
records.blind_answer: Bob blind-plays Finesse Position; Cathy then plays the Chop Moved card.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The Play Clue reading is explicitly turned off in this scope.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat rank 5 as direct Play Clue; Level 21 rule forbids that reading here.
records.mutation: Change to End-Game and the special interaction switches off.
records.noise: Solution shows post-Ignition knowledge without replaying the 5 clue or Bob's action.

records.source_rule: An Ignition blind-play is unrelated both to the clue and to proving the clued card playable.
records.learning_objective: Distinguish Ignition from Finesse and Bluff after the reveal.
records.critical_variable: Bob has already blind-played unrelated green 2 after a Replay DI trigger.
records.blind_answer: No connection or proof is required; that independence defines Ignition.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Requiring connection would turn the move into Finesse-like logic contrary to the definition.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Demand that green 2 connect to red 2; source explicitly says it need not.
records.mutation: Make the blind-play necessary to connect the clued card and the interpretation becomes Finesse-like instead.
records.noise: Question state now starts after green 2 has actually reached the stack.
